reason: The broad claim combines materially different comparison populations and outcome definitions. These choices change the estimated effect and, for contraband coding, change inference in 36.4% of paired specifications.
parent_hypothesis: Among searched stops in all recorded stops, Black subjects have a higher rate of any contraband hit than White subjects.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Among recorded stops in the stated 2002–2015 window where a search was conducted, and where subjects are classified strictly as Black or White, the Black-subject rate of direct-field contraband hits among complete cases is higher than the White-subject rate, using an unadjusted rate comparison with independent-stop uncertainty.
hypotheses.rationale: This isolates the strict Black-versus-White comparison and the direct complete-case outcome. The multiverse shows that race-group inclusion changes the estimated effect and inference, while direct-field coding and union coding change inference in 36.4% of paired specifications. Fixing the remaining analytic choices makes the claim testable without adding data.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Among recorded stops in the stated 2002–2015 window where a search was conducted, and where subjects are classified strictly as Black or White, the Black-subject rate of a drug-or-weapon contraband hit is higher than the White-subject rate, using an unadjusted rate comparison with independent-stop uncertainty.
hypotheses.rationale: This treats the union outcome as a separate estimand rather than combining it with direct-field contraband coding. The union specification has a materially different effect distribution from the direct-field specifications and changes inference in 60% of the reported pairwise comparisons with them, so it warrants its own directional hypothesis.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Among recorded stops in the stated 2002–2015 window where a search was conducted, and where Black and White subjects are classified using the raw race mapping, the Black-subject rate of direct-field contraband hits among complete cases is higher than the White-subject rate, using an unadjusted rate comparison with independent-stop uncertainty.
hypotheses.rationale: This separates the raw-race classification question from the strict Black-versus-White analytic-sample question. The race-classification choice produces a large change relative to the strict Black/White option and changes inference in some paired specifications, while the dataset contains the fields needed to test this raw-mapping version.
